result.summary: Data cleaning techniques are essential for ensuring the quality and accuracy of data, which is critical for making informed decisions and achieving reliable results in various fields such as business, healthcare, and research. These techniques involve identifying and correcting errors, handling missing values, and transforming data into a consistent format.
key_points: Handling missing values: replacing or imputing missing values to prevent bias and ensure data completeness
Data normalization: scaling numeric data to a common range to prevent differences in scales
Data transformation: converting data from one format to another to improve analysis and modeling
Error detection and correction: identifying and correcting errors such as outliers, duplicates, and inconsistencies
Data quality metrics: using metrics such as accuracy, completeness, and consistency to evaluate data quality
Automated data cleaning: using tools and algorithms to automate the data cleaning process
references: Rahm, E., & Do, H. H. (2000). Data cleaning: Problems and current approaches. IEEE Data Engineering Bulletin, 23(4), 3-13.
Dasu, T., & Johnson, T. (2003). Exploratory data mining and data cleaning. Wiley.
Kim, W., & Seo, J. (2017). Data cleaning techniques for big data analytics. International Journal of Distributed Sensor Networks, 13(6), 1550147717710704.

result.summary: Data transformation methods are techniques used to convert data from one format to another, enabling compatibility and analysis. These methods include aggregation, normalization, feature scaling, and data encoding, which are essential for data preprocessing and preparation for machine learning models and data visualization.
key_points: Aggregation: combining multiple values into a single value, such as sum or average
Normalization: scaling numeric data to a common range, usually between 0 and 1
Feature scaling: transforming data to have similar scales, often using standardization or min-max scaling
Data encoding: converting categorical data into numerical representations, such as one-hot encoding or label encoding
Data transformation techniques can be applied using various tools and programming languages, including Python, R, and SQL
references: Kuhn, M., & Johnson, K. (2019). Feature engineering and selection: A practical approach for predictive models. CRC Press.
James, G., Witten, D., Hastie, T., & Tibshirani, R. (2013). An introduction to statistical learning. Springer.

Data Transformation Methods. (n.d.). IBM Knowledge Center. Retrieved from https://www.ibm.com/support/knowledgecenter/en/SS6NHC/com.ibm.swg.im.dashdb.analytics.doc/doc/data_transformation_methods.html
